title: Mark Zuckerberg says billions will have a personal AI agent within five years

content_html:
Mark Zuckerberg thinks almost everyone will soon have an AI that works for them. On Meta’s second-quarter earnings call on 29 July, he predicted that within five years “billions of people” will each have “a personal agent that understands your goals,” handling their finances, health, relationships, and homes.

It was the boldest version yet of a pitch he has been sharpening for months. Mark Zuckerberg has cast personal AI agents as the next mass-market computing platform, and Meta’s own apps, WhatsApp and Messenger, as the place most people will meet them.

The prediction is also a business plan. Meta already runs AI agents for companies on its messaging apps, reaching more than a million business users this quarter, and the consumer version is meant to become a revenue stream large enough to justify the money going in.

That money is the uncomfortable backdrop. Meta’s free cash flow fell 91% in the quarter, to $784 million, and its Reality Labs division lost another $4.6 billion, bringing its cumulative losses since 2021 to roughly $88 billion.

The infrastructure bill keeps climbing on top of that. Meta and BlackRock announced a $14 billion data-centre partnership in El Paso this quarter, one more sign that the company is building for the agent future long before the revenue exists to pay for it.

Investors were not soothed by the vision. Meta’s stock fell nearly 10% after the results, a sign that Wall Street is, for now, more moved by the collapsing cash flow than by the promise of an agent in every pocket.

He has a history of declaring the next platform early, from the metaverse to AI, and of spending vast sums to be first, with results that have ranged from dominant to disappointing.

His own agents have not all arrived on schedule. Zuckerberg conceded earlier this year that Meta’s AI-agent progress was slower than he had hoped, which makes the confidence of a five-year, billions-of-users forecast a notable bet on a sharp acceleration.

He is, at least, using the products himself. Zuckerberg has talked about building a personal assistant to handle his own executive load, a hint of the everyday, do-things-for-you agent he expects the rest of the world to adopt.

The vision is coherent, whatever its odds. If agents become the way people manage money, health, and household admin, whoever owns the agent owns an extraordinary position, which is why Meta, OpenAI, and Google are all racing for the same ground.

He is not the only one. OpenAI, Google, and a wave of startups are making near-identical promises, which lends the idea momentum but also means that being right about agents is not the same as winning them.

The catch is the same for all of them. Building agents that reliably act on someone’s behalf, with their money and their data, is far harder than building a chatbot that answers questions, and trust is not something a demo can manufacture.

For Meta specifically, there is a credibility gap to close. This is a company fighting lawsuits over how its existing products affect users, now asking those same users to hand an AI agent the keys to their finances and health.

Regulators may have views on that too. Giving an agent access to someone’s bank account and medical history raises exactly the privacy questions Meta is already fighting, which could slow the very future Zuckerberg is describing.

Mark Zuckerberg’s answer is to spend his way through the doubt. Meta’s capital budget is heading toward $145 billion, a bet that if it builds the infrastructure and the models, the agents, and the billions of users, will follow.

The five-year clock is now running, at least rhetorically. Zuckerberg has named a number and a date; the market’s tepid response suggests it would rather see the agents than hear about them, and the gap between the two is where the next few years will be decided.

content_html_zh:
马克·扎克伯格认为，几乎每个人很快都会拥有适合他们的人工智能。 在 7 月 29 日 Meta 的第二季度财报电话会议上，他预测五年内“数十亿人”将各自拥有“一位了解你目标的个人代理人”，负责处理他们的财务、健康、人际关系和家庭事务。

这是他几个月来不断完善的方案中迄今为止最大胆的版本。 马克·扎克伯格将个人人工智能代理视为下一个大众市场计算平台，并将 Meta 自己的应用程序 WhatsApp 和 Messenger 视为大多数人会见人工智能代理的地方。

预测也是一个商业计划。 Meta 已经在其消息应用程序上为公司运行人工智能代理，本季度覆盖了超过 100 万商业用户，而消费者版本将成为一个足够大的收入来源，足以证明投入的资金是合理的。

这笔钱是令人不安的背景。 Meta 的自由现金流在本季度下降了 91%，至 7.84 亿美元，其 Reality Labs 部门又损失了 46 亿美元，使其自 2021 年以来的累计损失达到约 880 亿美元。

除此之外，基础设施费用还在不断攀升。 Meta 和贝莱德本季度宣布在埃尔帕索建立价值 140 亿美元的数据中心合作伙伴关系，这又一个迹象表明，该公司早在收入支付之前就正在为代理的未来进行建设。

投资者并没有因这一愿景而安抚。 财报公布后，Meta 的股价下跌了近 10%，这表明华尔街目前更多的是受到现金流崩溃的影响，而不是每个口袋里都有代理人的承诺。

他有很早就宣布下一个平台的历史，从元宇宙到人工智能，并花费大量资金来成为第一，其结果从主导到令人失望。

他自己的特工还没有全部按期抵达。 扎克伯格今年早些时候承认，Meta 的人工智能代理进展速度比他希望的要慢，这使得五年后数十亿用户的信心明显押注于大幅加速。

至少他自己正在使用这些产品。 扎克伯格曾谈到要建立一名私人助理来处理自己的行政事务，这是他希望世界其他地方采用的那种每天为你做事的代理人的暗示。

无论可能性如何，愿景都是连贯的。 如果代理成为人们管理金钱、健康和家庭管理的方式，那么谁拥有代理，谁就拥有了非凡的地位，这就是为什么 Meta、OpenAI 和 Google 都在同一个领域竞相竞争。

他不是唯一一个。 OpenAI、谷歌和一波初创公司正在做出几乎相同的承诺，这为这一想法提供了动力，但也意味着正确对待代理并不等于赢得代理。

他们所有人的收获都是一样的。 构建能够利用资金和数据可靠地代表某人行事的代理，比构建回答问题的聊天机器人要困难得多，而且信任不是演示可以制造的。

特别是对于 Meta 来说，存在着可信度差距需要弥合。 这家公司正在就其现有产品如何影响用户提起诉讼，现在要求这些用户将其财务和健康的钥匙交给人工智能代理。

监管机构可能对此也有看法。 让代理人访问某人的银行账户和病史恰恰引发了 Meta 已经在努力解决的隐私问题，这可能会减缓扎克伯格所描述的未来。

马克·扎克伯格的答案是用自己的方式消除疑虑。 Meta 的资本预算即将达到 1450 亿美元，押注如果它建立了基础设施和模型，那么代理和数十亿用户就会跟进。

五年的时钟现在正在运行，至少在口头上是这样。 扎克伯格已经指定了一个号码和一个日期；市场反应不温不火，表明它宁愿看到代理商，也不愿听到他们的消息，而两者之间的差距将决定未来几年的发展。
